h: שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל, מַאֲמָר ח׳ Shabbos HaGadol — Maamar Ches
Eliyahu Before the Great and Awesome Day: Nisan Redemption and Shabbos Teshuvah

p: שַׁבָּת זוֹ נִקְרָא שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל
This Shabbos is called Shabbos HaGadol
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר
along the lines of what is said
(מַלְאָכִי ג', כ"ג):
(Malachi 3:23):
הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי שֹׁלֵחַ לָכֶם אֵת אֵלִיָּה הַנָּבִיא לִפְנֵי בּוֹא יוֹם ה' הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא,
"Behold, I send you Eliyahu the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome day of Hashem,"
וְהַיְינוּ יְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ.
which refers to the Days of Mashiach.
שֶׁאָז יִרְאוּ עַיִן בְּעַיִן שֶׁכָּל הַסַּבְלָנוּת שֶׁסָּבְלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּגָּלוּיוֹת
For then they will see eye to eye that all the suffering Israel endured in the exiles
הָיָה רַק חֶסֶד וְרַחֲמִים, כְּדֵי שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִזְכּוּ לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ.
was purely kindness and mercy, so that through it they would merit the Days of Mashiach.
וְזֶה מִדַּת חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם, גְּדוּלָּה, וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ אוֹמְרִים בְּבִרְכַּת אָבוֹת "הַגָּדוֹל",
And this is the attribute of "Kindness to Avraham," Gedulah, corresponding to which we say "the Great" in the Blessing of the Patriarchs,
וְרַחֲמִים מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ "הַנּוֹרָא"
and mercy is the attribute of our father Yaakov, peace be upon him, corresponding to which is "the Awesome"
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' ע"ט.),
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 79a),
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
and along the lines of what they said in the Gemara
(יוֹמָא ס"ט:)
(Yoma 69b)
אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ:
regarding the Men of the Great Assembly, who said:
וְאֵלּוּ הֵן נוֹרְאוֹתָיו, שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא מוֹרָאוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי.
"And these are His awesome deeds, for were it not for the awe of the Holy One, blessed is He, etc."
רַק שֶׁאָז בַּגָּלוּת אָמְרוּ בֶּאֱמוּנָה,
Only then, in exile, they declared this through faith,
וְלִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ יִרְאוּ זֶה מְפוֹרָשׁ,
whereas in the Days of Mashiach they will see this openly,
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי נִקְרָא יְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ יוֹם ה' הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא.
and therefore the Days of Mashiach are called "the great and awesome day of Hashem."
וְכָל שֶׁלֹּא בָּא מֵאֶתְמוֹל אֵלִיָּהוּ לֹא אָתֵי מְשִׁיחָא,
And whenever Eliyahu did not come the day before, Mashiach does not come [that day],
שֶׁמֵּהַאי טַעְמָא מוּתָּר בְּשַׁבָּת בְּיַיִן,
for which reason a Nazirite is permitted wine on Shabbos,
שֶׁמּוּבְטָח לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֵין אֵלִיָּהוּ בָּא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵּי,
as Israel are assured that Eliyahu does not come on Erev Shabbos, etc.,
כִּדְאִיתָא בְּעֵירוּבִין
as stated in Eruvin
וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין תְּחוּמִין לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה,
and according to the opinion that Shabbos boundaries do not apply above ten handbreadths,
אָתֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ בְּשַׁבָּת וּבְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת מִיָּד נִגְאָלִין.
Eliyahu can come on Shabbos, and on Motza'ei Shabbos they are immediately redeemed.
וּבְנִיסָן עֲתִידִין לְהִגָּאֵל לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
And in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed according to Rabbi Yehoshua
(רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה י"א.).
(Rosh Hashanah 11a).
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ דְּאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים:
And we have already explained that "both these and those are the words of the living God":
וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְשִׁיטָּתוֹ
Rabbi Eliezer follows his own view
(סַנְהֶדְרִין צ"ז:)
(Sanhedrin 97b)
שֶׁהַגְּאוּלָּה עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה דַּוְקָא, לָכֵן הַזְּמַן לְהַגְּאוּלָּה בְּתִשְׁרֵי;
that redemption comes specifically through repentance, so the time for redemption is in Tishrei;
וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְשִׁיטָּתוֹ
and Rabbi Yehoshua follows his own view
(ibid.)
לֹא בִּתְשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵּי,
"not through repentance, etc.,"
הַזְּמַן בְּנִיסָן כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה גְּאוּלַּת מִצְרַיִם בְּחֶסֶד ה'.
so the time is in Nisan, just as the redemption from Egypt took place through Hashem's kindness.
וּבְוַדַּאי אֵין הַפֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁיִּגָּאֲלוּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּתְשׁוּבָה,
And certainly the meaning is not that they will be redeemed without repentance;
רַק שֶׁאַף אִם לֹא יָשׁוּבוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצִּדָּם,
rather, even if Israel do not repent on their own,
ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מַעֲמִיד לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ וְכוּלֵּי וּמַחֲזִירָם בִּתְשׁוּבָה בְּחַסְדּוֹ
Hashem, may He be blessed, sets up a king over them, etc., and brings them back in repentance through His kindness
(כִּדְאִיתָא שָׁם).
(as stated there).
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּסוֹף קִינוֹת
And this is what is said at the end of Eichah
(אֵיכָה ה', כ"א):
(Eichah 5:21):
הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ ה' אֵלֶיךָ וְנָשׁוּבָה וְגוֹמֵר,
"Bring us back to You, Hashem, and we shall return, etc."
שֶׁזֶּה הַמְכוּוָן בְּכָל הַגָּלוּיוֹת, וְזֶה יְסוֹד הַקִּינוֹת,
for this is the intent in all the exiles, and this is the foundation of the lamentations,
וְאַף שֶׁיֵּשׁ פָּסוּק אַחֲרָיו, חוֹזְרִין וּמְסַיְּימִין בְּפָסוּק זֶה.
and even though there is another verse after it, we repeat and conclude with this verse.
וְלָזֶה הַזְּמַן בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁקּוֹדֶם פֶּסַח,
And the opportune time for this is on the Shabbos before Pesach,
דְּשַׁבָּת זְמַן תְּשׁוּבָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
because Shabbos is a time of repentance, as it is said
(תְּהִלִּים צ"ב, ב'):
(Tehillim 92:2):
טוֹב לְהוֹדוֹת לַה',
"It is good to give thanks (and confess) to Hashem,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר
along the lines of what is said
(מִשְׁלֵי כ"ח, י"ג):
(Mishlei 28:13):
מוֹדֶה וְעֹזֵב יְרֻחָם
"He who confesses and forsakes [his sins] will obtain mercy"
(פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק י"ט),
(Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer, Chapter 19),
וּבְמִדְרָשׁ
and in the Midrash
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה כ"ב, י"ג):
(Bereishis Rabbah 22:13):
כָּךְ כֹּחָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵּי מִזְמוֹר שִׁיר לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת וְגוֹמֵר,
"Such is the power of repentance, etc., 'A Psalm, a Song for the Shabbos day, etc.,'"
וְאָז יִזְכּוּ לְהִגָּאֵל בְּחַג הַפֶּסַח כִּימֵי צֵאתֵנוּ מִמִּצְרָיִם.
and then they will merit to be redeemed on the festival of Pesach, "as in the days of our going forth from Egypt."
וּבַגְּמָרָא
And in the Gemara
(שַׁבָּת קי"ח.)
(Shabbos 118a)
שֶׁהַמְּקַיֵּים שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת נִיצּוֹל מִשָּׁלֹשׁ פּוּרְעָנִיּוֹת: מֵחֶבְלוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ...
it states that one who fulfills the three Shabbos meals is saved from three punishments: from the birth pangs of Mashiach...
כְּתִיב הָכָא "יוֹם" וּכְתִיב הָתָם "יוֹם ה' הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא".
it is written here "day" and it is written there "the great and awesome day of Hashem."
וְהַיְינוּ דְּחֶבְלֵי מָשִׁיחַ הוּא קוֹדֶם בִּיאַת הַמָּשִׁיחַ שֶׁהוּא יוֹם ה' גָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא,
That is, the birth pangs of Mashiach occur prior to the coming of Mashiach, which is the great and awesome day of Hashem,
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁמְּקַיֵּים שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת נִיצּוֹל מֵחֶבְלֵי מָשִׁיחַ.
and by fulfilling the three meals one is saved from the birth pangs of Mashiach.
וְחַג הַפֶּסַח נִקְרָא יוֹם ה' הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא, שֶׁהֵם מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם וְיַעֲקֹב:
And the festival of Pesach is called "the great and awesome day of Hashem," which are the attributes of Avraham and Yaakov:
הַגָּדוֹל הוּא מִדַּת אַהֲבָה שֶׁנֶּגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
"the Great" is the attribute of love, corresponding to our father Avraham, peace be upon him,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל;
to whom the Egyptian exile was foretold and that "afterward they shall go out with great wealth";
וְהַנּוֹרָא — שֶׁתַּכְלִית יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם:
and "the Awesome"—for the ultimate purpose of the Exodus from Egypt was:
בְּהוֹצִיאֲךָ אֶת הָעָם... תַּעַבְדוּן אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים וְגוֹמֵר,
"When you bring the people out... you shall serve God, etc.,"
וְאָז יִקָּבַע מִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and then the attribute of love is permanently fixed in the heart of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם וְכוּלֵּי תּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת וְכוּלֵּי אוֹתָנוּ לִמַּדְתָּ,
as we say, "With an eternal love, etc., Torah and mitzvos, etc., You have taught us"
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַנּוֹרָא, שְׁלֵימוּ דְּכוּלְּהוּ,
and this is the attribute of our father Yaakov, peace be upon him, "the Awesome," the perfection of them all,
שֶׁיִּקָּבַע הָאַהֲבָה בְּלִבָּם לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד,
that love be fixed in their hearts forevermore,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
as it is said
(מִיכָה ז', כ'):
(Michah 7:20):
תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב,
"You will give truth to Yaakov,"
וּכְתִיב
and it is written
(מִשְׁלֵי י"ב, י"ט):
(Mishlei 12:19):
שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד.
"A truthful lip shall be established forever."
וְהַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁקּוֹדֶם חַג הַפֶּסַח הִיא לִפְנֵי בּוֹא יוֹם ה' הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא,
And the Shabbos before the festival of Pesach is "before the coming of the great and awesome day of Hashem,"
וְהַזְּמַן בּוֹ לִזְכּוֹת לְשַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה וּתְשׁוּבָה עִילָּאָה וְלִהְיוֹת מִיָּד נִגְאָל לְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת,
and it is the opportune time to merit Supernal Shabbos and supernal repentance, and to be immediately redeemed on Motza'ei Shabbos
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי נִקְרָא שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל
and therefore it is called Shabbos HaGadol
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל מַאֲמָר ו').
(as explained above in Maamar 6).

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 79a (Yisro) — "'The work of Hashem, that it is awesome (nora)' (Shemos 34:10). What is 'awesome'? Rabbi Elazar said: the perfection of all, as it says (Devarim 10:17), 'the great, the mighty and the awesome God.' What is 'the awesome'? This is Yaakov, and it is written, 'Yaakov was a tam (whole) man,' as the Targum renders, a perfect man, perfect in all."

paragraphs.text: Yoma 69b — "Yirmeyahu came and said: Foreigners are carousing in His sanctuary; where are His awesome deeds? He did not say 'awesome'... Then they [the Men of the Great Assembly] came and said:... These are His awesome deeds: were it not for the awe of the Holy One, blessed is He, how could one nation survive among the nations?" Rashi: all the nations gathered to destroy them, and He preserved them.

Israel have already been assured that Eliyahu will not come either on Erev Shabbos or on Erev Yom Tov, because of the bother." Rashi: because they would leave their Shabbos preparations and go out to greet him.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 11a–b — "Rabbi Yehoshua says: In Nisan the world was created... in Nisan they were redeemed, and in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed." (11b:) "From where? The verse says (Shemos 12:42), 'It is a night of watching (leil shimurim)': a night guarded and coming from the six days of Creation." Rashi: "guarded and coming" — for the redemption.

The verse says (Shemos 12:42), 'It is a night of watching (leil shimurim)': a night guarded and coming from the six days of Creation." Rashi: "guarded and coming" — for the redemption.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Beshalach 6 — “Therefore, of these two Shabbosos, in Nisan and in Tishrei, the one in Nisan is called Shabbos HaGadol, following Rabbi Yehoshua that in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed; that is, if the redemption comes from Hashem's side, like the redemption from Egypt, in line with his view that it is not through repentance and good deeds. It is called Shabbos HaGadol after the attribute of Gedulah, kindness from Hashem. And in Tishrei, following Rabbi Eliezer, that is, if the redemption comes through repentance, it is called Shabbos Teshuvah or Shuvah.” Connection: The same pairing of Tishrei with repentance and Nisan with Hashem's kindness; it carries the pairing over to the names of the two Shabbosos, deriving "HaGadol" from Gedulah-kindness and "Shuvah" from repentance.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 97b — "Rabbi Eliezer says: If Israel repent they are redeemed, and if not they are not redeemed. Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: If they do not repent they are not redeemed? Rather, the Holy One, blessed is He, sets up a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's, Israel repent, and He brings them back to the good." Another baraisa: "'You shall be redeemed not with money' (Yeshayahu 52:3): not with repentance and good deeds." Rashi: even without repentance they are redeemed.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Machshavos Charutz 7 — “Rabbi Eliezer, who holds that in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed, follows his view that redemption depends on repentance; and Rabbi Yehoshua follows his reasoning, that the Holy One, blessed is He, sets up over them a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's, and Israel repent. That is, the very force of the subjugation is what brings about the awakening from Above, to light up in their hearts the stirring of repentance. The harsh king like Haman is in Adar, and afterward in Nisan they are redeemed.” Connection: The same reading that Rabbi Yehoshua's Nisan redemption still passes through a repentance Hashem Himself awakens; it adds that the harsh subjugation is itself that awakening from Above, and sets it on the calendar: Haman in Adar, redemption in Nisan.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 118a — "Whoever fulfills the three meals on Shabbos is saved from three calamities: the birth pangs of Mashiach, the judgment of Gehinnom, and the war of Gog and Magog. From the birth pangs of Mashiach: it is written here 'day,' and there, 'before the coming of the day of Hashem' (Malachi 3:23)." Rashi: "chevlei" as in the pangs of childbirth (cf. Kesubos 112b).

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Shabbos HaGadol 5634 — “Shabbos HaGadol is also like Shabbos Shuvah, only it is in the aspect of love: every person must return to the Blessed One out of the greatness of the kindness He did with us when He took us out of Egypt and chose us to be His people and inheritance. This is Shabbos HaGadol, that a person returns in teshuvah through His greatness, blessed is He. The Holy One, blessed is He, redeemed us before we entered the fiftieth gate of impurity.” Connection: The Sefas Emes likewise makes the Shabbos before Pesach a Shabbos of teshuvah and ties its name to Divine greatness and kindness; he adds the contrast with Shabbos Shuvah, a return born of love rather than fear, and frames the Egyptian redemption as coming before Israel had sunk past recovery.
